concept.name: Property-Based Testing

relationships.description: Connects Property-Based Testing to contract testing in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Property-based testing replaces hand-picked example inputs with randomized, strategy-driven input generation and automatic shrinking to prove invariants across thousands of edge cases.
spark.keyTakeaway: Define what must always hold true (round-trips, conservation laws, idempotence), let Hypothesis or jqwik generate adversarial inputs, and let the shrinker hand you the minimal 2-line reproducer.

concept.whyItMatters: Example-based unit tests only verify the edge cases a developer remembers to write, leaving parsers, financial ledgers, state machines, and serializers exposed to empty strings, Unicode surrogates, integer overflows, and rare interleavings. Property-based testing explores the combinatorial input space systematically and automatically minimizes any failing input to its simplest counterexample.
whenToUse: Testing parsers, serializers, encoders, and compression codecs using round-trip invariants like decode(encode(x)) == x.
Validating financial ledgers, billing allocators, and scheduling algorithms against conservation laws (sum of splits equals total) and monotonicity.
Verifying stateful APIs, caches, and concurrent state machines against a simple in-memory reference model using stateful rule-based testing.
whenNotToUse: UI layout, visual styling, or third-party SaaS integration flows where generating 500 random permutations per test run is slow and brittle.
Simple CRUD endpoints with trivial pass-through validation where writing an invariant just duplicates the implementation logic.
Security-critical binary fuzzing of C/C++ memory parsers where coverage-guided fuzzers like AFL++ or libFuzzer outperform black-box property generators.
keyPoints: Generators (strategies) compose primitives like integers, UTF-8 text, and lists into domain objects with explicit constraints.
Shrinking is the killer feature: when a 40-element list fails, Hypothesis or fast-check bisects and simplifies it down to a minimal case like [0, -1].
Good properties avoid re-implementing the function under test; instead they check algebraic laws (idempotence, commutativity, round-trip, or oracle equivalence).
Saved failure databases (such as .hypothesis/examples) replay every past counterexample deterministically before generating new random cases.
Stateful property testing (e.g., Hypothesis RuleBasedStateMachine) discovers multi-step sequence bugs such as insert -> evict -> delete.

examples.title: Penny-Accurate Invoice Split Allocator
examples.scenario: A billing service splits an integer total_cents across N weighted line items using a custom rounding algorithm, tested with Hypothesis st.integers(0, 10_000_000) and st.lists(st.floats(0.01, 1.0), min_size=1, max_size=20).
examples.outcome: Hypothesis discovers a floating-point weight sum where remainder pennies are dropped, shrinks the failure to total_cents=100 and 3 equal weights, and catches the bug before production.

examples.title: Canonical URL-Safe Token Codec
examples.scenario: A custom base64url + JSON token serializer in Python is tested for round-trip fidelity across arbitrary Unicode dictionaries using st.recursive() strategies.
examples.outcome: The generator produces lone UTF-16 surrogate characters and embedded null bytes that crash the C-backed JSON parser; shrinking isolates the exact 1-character payload 'U+D800'.

tradeOffs.pro: Runs 100 to 1,000+ diverse cases per test function automatically without manual test-case authoring.
tradeOffs.con: Increases CI suite runtime if heavy I/O or database calls are placed inside the @given loop.

tradeOffs.pro: Uncovers unknown unknowns such as NaN propagation, timezone DST gaps, and off-by-one boundaries.
tradeOffs.con: Requires deeper mathematical thinking to formulate non-tautological invariants instead of hardcoded expected outputs.

tradeOffs.pro: Persisting PRNG seeds and example databases guarantees exact regression replay for discovered bugs.
tradeOffs.con: Newly discovered random failures on unrelated PRs can look like flaky tests if teams do not pin or triage seeds.

failureModes.name: Tautological Property (Mirroring Implementation)
failureModes.description: The test re-implements the exact same formula as the production code and asserts equality, passing even when both are wrong.
failureModes.mitigation: Use independent invariants (round-trip, conservation, sorting order) or compare against a simpler brute-force O(n^2) oracle.

failureModes.name: Over-Filtered Strategy Starvation
failureModes.description: Using assume() or .filter() with a rare predicate causes the generator to discard 99% of inputs and abort with Unsatisfiable.
failureModes.mitigation: Construct valid inputs directly via st.builds() or flatmap() rather than generating garbage and filtering it out.

failureModes.name: Stateful Test Contamination
failureModes.description: Mutating shared global state or database rows across generated iterations causes false positives that fail to shrink cleanly.
failureModes.mitigation: Reset state per iteration or isolate each run inside a rolled-back transaction or fresh in-memory instance.

failureModes.name: Unbounded Deadline Timeouts
failureModes.description: Default 200ms per-example deadlines in Hypothesis trigger spurious DeadlineExceeded errors on cold JIT warmup or loaded CI runners.
failureModes.mitigation: Set @settings(deadline=None) for I/O-adjacent tests and keep property functions pure and in-memory.

commonMistakes: Putting live network or database calls inside @given without mocking or in-memory fakes, slowing 200 examples to 30+ seconds.
Ignoring the .hypothesis/examples directory in CI artifacts instead of committing or caching discovered regression seeds.
Writing 100% random generators without boundary biasing, missing 0, -1, empty lists, and MAX_INT unless the framework injects them.
Asserting exact floating-point equality (==) instead of math.isclose() or integer minor-unit arithmetic.
Disabling shrinking or failing to read the shrunk minimal counterexample at the bottom of the test traceback.

sections.content:
## The idea

Traditional unit tests assert single points in an input space: `assert sort([3, 1, 2]) == [1, 2, 3]`. Property-based testing (pioneered by Haskell's QuickCheck and realized in Python's Hypothesis, Java's jqwik, and TypeScript's fast-check) instead asserts universal truths that must hold across *all* valid inputs drawn from a typed generator: `len(sort(xs)) == len(xs)`, `is_non_decreasing(sort(xs))`, and `Counter(sort(xs)) == Counter(xs)`.

Crucially, property-based testing is not mere random fuzzing. Modern engines pair structured input strategies with **integrated shrinking**: the moment a 200-element random input breaks an invariant, the runner replays simpler, smaller sub-choices along its internal byte/choice tree until it hands the developer the smallest possible counterexample.

## Concrete walkthrough

Consider testing a run-length encoder `rle_encode(s)` and decoder `rle_decode(encoded)` in Python with Hypothesis:

1. **Define the strategy**: `@given(st.text(alphabet=st.characters(), min_size=0, max_size=200))`.
2. **Assert the round-trip invariant**: `assert rle_decode(rle_encode(s)) == s`.
3. **Hit an edge case**: Hypothesis generates `s = "a00b"` or `"12x"` when the naive encoder writes `"1a201b"` without escaping digits.
4. **Automatic shrinking**: Instead of dumping a 180-character random Unicode string, Hypothesis shrinks the failing input down to `s = "0"` in ~12 steps, immediately exposing that digits in the input collide with run-length counts in the output.

data.title: Property-Based Test Execution & Shrinking Loop

edges.label: 100-500 structured inputs
edges.title: Generate Candidate Input
edges.description: Draws typed values biased toward 0, empty collections, extremes, and previously failing seeds.

edges.label: Actual output / state
edges.title: Execute Target Logic
edges.description: Runs the function or state-machine transition sequence under test.

edges.label: AssertionError / exception
edges.title: Detect Invariant Violation
edges.description: Flags any broken algebraic law, crash, or divergence from the reference oracle.

edges.label: Smaller choice sequence
edges.title: Shrink Choice Tree
edges.description: Deletes elements, zeroes integers, and simplifies characters to find a strictly smaller failing case.

edges.label: Verify minimal repro
edges.title: Validate Minimal Counterexample
edges.description: Re-runs the shrunk candidate until no simpler failing input can be found, then saves the seed.

data.caption: Hypothesis and modern PBT frameworks shrink the underlying random choice stream rather than raw domain values, guaranteeing every shrunk candidate still satisfies strategy preconditions.

sections.content:
## High-leverage invariant patterns

The hardest part of property-based testing is writing assertions that do not simply duplicate the code under test. Five proven patterns cover most production systems:

- **Round-trip (Encode/Decode)**: `parse(serialize(obj)) == obj` for JSON, Protobuf, SQL ASTs, or URL query builders.
- **Oracle Equivalence**: Compare a fast, complex algorithm (e.g., SIMD B-tree or parallel merge) against a slow, obviously correct 10-line reference implementation.
- **Idempotence**: `normalize(normalize(x)) == normalize(x)` for deduplicators, database upserts, and cache warmers.
- **Conservation / Metrical Bounds**: Total money before and after transfers is unchanged; output list length matches input length.
- **Stateful Model Checking**: Generate random sequences of `put`, `get`, `delete`, and `ttl_expire` against an LRU cache and assert every step matches a plain Python `dict`.

## Framework & fuzzing comparison

| Tool | Language | Shrinking Mechanism | Stateful Testing | Best Fit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hypothesis** | Python | Integrated choice-sequence shrinking | `RuleBasedStateMachine` | Data pipelines, APIs, ML preprocessing |
| **jqwik** | Java / Kotlin | Integrated type-aware shrinking | `@State` action chains | JVM domain invariants, JUnit 5 suites |
| **fast-check** | TypeScript / JS | Integrated stream shrinking | `fc.modelRun` | Frontend state, parsers, reducers |
| **proptest** | Rust | Value-tree shrinking | `prop_state_machine!` | Zero-copy codecs, lock-free structs |
| **AFL++ / libFuzzer** | C / C++ / Go | Corpus minimization (`afl-cmin`) | Grammar mutators | Memory-safety & crash hunting via coverage |

## Failure modes

Property-based suites fail silently or become team friction points in four recurring ways:

- **Filter starvation**: Chaining `.filter(lambda x: x > 100 and is_prime(x))` causes the generator to hit its discard limit and fail with `Unsatisfiable`. Always construct valid domains directly.
- **Non-deterministic SUTs**: Testing code that reads `datetime.now()` or unordered `set` iteration produces flaky failures that the shrinker cannot reproduce.
- **Slow I/O inside the loop**: Running 200 examples against a real Postgres container takes 15+ seconds per test; use SQLite/fakes in the property loop and keep 2–3 integration tests for real Postgres.
- **Forgotten example databases**: If CI discards `.hypothesis/examples` after every build, previously caught edge cases may not be replayed first on future runs.

sections.eyebrow: 06 / Tuning profiles for local vs. CI
sections.content:
## Tuning profiles for local vs. CI

Use **profiles** (`settings.register_profile`) so developers get fast feedback locally while CI runs deeper searches:

- **Dev profile**: `max_examples=50`, fast feedback in `<500 ms` per test.
- **CI PR profile**: `max_examples=250`, `derandomize=True` (optional for strict PR determinism) or shared example cache.
- **Nightly soak profile**: `max_examples=5_000` to `10_000` with `HealthCheck` tuned to hunt rare multi-step state machine bugs overnight without blocking pull requests.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Identify at least one algebraic invariant (round-trip, idempotence, conservation, or reference oracle) before writing the test.
- [ ] Build valid inputs constructively with `st.builds()` / `Arbitraries` instead of heavy `.filter()` predicates.
- [ ] Inject explicit clock/PRNG dependencies so the system under test is 100% deterministic for a given input.
- [ ] Add `@example(...)` decorators for every shrunk counterexample found in production or CI so it is permanently pinned in code.
- [ ] Configure separate `dev` (50 examples) and `nightly` (5,000+ examples) profiles.

interviewProblems.title: Property-Based Testing
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on Property-Based Testing. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Property-based testing replaces hand-picked example inputs with randomized, strategy-driven input generation and automatic shrinking to prove invariants across thousands of edge cases.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: Invariant Oracle applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Shrinker & Seed DB.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Shrinker & Seed DB experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Use independent invariants (round-trip, conservation, sorting order) or compare against a simpler brute-force O(n^2) oracle.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Define what must always hold true (round-trips, conservation laws, idempotence), let Hypothesis or jqwik generate adversarial inputs, and let the shrinker hand you the minimal 2-line reproducer.
Avoid trap: Putting live network or database calls inside @given without mocking or in-memory fakes, slowing 200 examples to 30+ seconds.
Avoid trap: Ignoring the .hypothesis/examples directory in CI artifacts instead of committing or caching discovered regression seeds.
When to reach for it: Testing parsers, serializers, encoders, and compression codecs using round-trip invariants like decode(encode(x)) == x.
When to reach for it: Validating financial ledgers, billing allocators, and scheduling algorithms against conservation laws (sum of splits equals total) and monotonicity.

putItTogether.title: Putting Property Based Testing Together
putItTogether.summary: Define what must always hold true (round-trips, conservation laws, idempotence), let Hypothesis or jqwik generate adversarial inputs, and let the shrinker hand you the minimal 2-line reproducer.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Property Based Testing before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Hypothesis discovers a floating-point weight sum where remainder pennies are dropped, shrinks the failure to total_cents=100 and 3 equal weights, and catches the bug before production.
